extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / Fellows of the Royal Society (17th-century scientific readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and reporting empirical observations, experiments, case reports, and antiquarian/astronomical notes for a learned scientific journal (Philosophical Transactions). Emphasizes methods of observation, experimental tests, measurements, specimen description, and arguments from analogy and prior reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguing spontaneous firing of pyrites by analogy and multiple instances
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be objected, that no body is kindled by itself: but it seems to be apparently otherwise; for vegetables will heat and take fire of themselves, as in the frequent instance of wet hay; and animals are naturally on fire, and men also sufficiently evince it, when in a fever; and among minerals, the pyrites, both in gross and in vapour, is actually fired of its own accord; and damps naturally take fire of themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims of spontaneous mineral ignition by citing analogous natural phenomena (wet hay, fevers, damps) and by showing that both solid and vapour forms of the mineral exhibit ignition. Use global examples (e.g., volcanoes) and chemical/physical evidence (sulphur sublimation, presence of loadstone in ejected cinders) to reinforce the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of empirical extraordinary instances to support meteorological hypotheses (lightning/thunder from pyrites)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two sorts of instances... which very much favour the opinion ... that thunder and lightning owe their matter to the sole breath of the pyrites: ... iron having fallen in great masses, and also in powder after the manner of rain... lightning being magnetic: ... a petrified piece of ash, which is magnetic; that is, the pyrites in succo; which makes it probable it may be magnetic also in vapour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing a theory about thunder and lightning originating from a substance, marshal historical and observable instances (reports of 'iron rain', magnetic residues after lightning, magnetic petrified ash) and, where possible, produce or reference physical specimens. Treat prodigious instances cautiously but bring them under inquiry to either confirm or confute for posterity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for reporting shipboard lightning effects and compass anomalies
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of the Albemarle: thunder storm burned the main-topsail, split the main cap, rent the mast; something from the clouds fell on the stern, a bituminous matter, smelling like fired gun-powder, continued burning; at night compasses were changed (north pointed south in binnacle; other compasses showed different deviations); a compass exposed to air lost its virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report anomalous physical events with precise date/location, sequence of damage, sensory description of falling matter (smell, persistence of burning), detailed observations of instrument behavior (compass deviations, multiple instruments compared), and follow-up tests (behavior after exposure to air). Include where possible later testing or transport notes to show change over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental program and protocols for studying urinary calculi (therapeutic part)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments to be made, relating to the Therapeutic Part. — To discover innocent menstruums that may dissolve the stone. — To examine the condition of the urine sometime before a paroxysm, both as to its specific gravity and contents. — And also during the paroxysm... — To inquire into the nature of nephritic medicines. — To examine lithontriptics, so as to exclude those from that class and character, which have no relative virtue that way: and to lessen the catalogue of those mistaken specifics. — To inquire into the nature of the hop, which is so much and perhaps innocently condemned for its aptness to generate the stone. — To explain the manner of the operations of some medicines, which though they are not lithontriptics, yet may be good nephritics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experimental and observational work addressing dissolution agents, urine chemistry before/during attacks (specific gravity and contents), pharmacological nature of nephritic medicines, and critical evaluation of purported lithontriptics to exclude ineffective preparations. Include physiological correlates and proposed mechanisms of action for medicines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical/chemical and hydrostatic tests to determine composition of calculi and bone
rubrics_metrics.description: Having cleared the bone of marrow and fat by boiling it in water, I distilled it, and obtained about 3 drams and a half, from an ounce of bone, of a volatile liquor impregnated with salt... The caput mortuum, as to weight, very consonant; and also could extract no manner of salt from it. ... few acids will dissolve it, excepting those that are nitrous... Experiments: Several stones of the bladder and kidneys were distilled; and all afforded volatile urinous salts, which ferment on any acids. — Petrified water affords only fresh and clear water on distillation. — Calculi examined hydrostatically, were found in proportion to their bulk of water, as 5 to 4. — We weighed flint, crystal, petrified water ... bones hydrostatically; and found them twice as heavy as their bulk of water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distillation, acid reactivity tests (including nitrous acids), and hydrostatic weighing to compare specific gravities. Compare caput mortuum weights, solubility profiles, volatile products (urinous salts), and relative densities against known materials (bone, flint) to infer composition of calculi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational methodology for sunspot tracking and prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: By the observed meridional distances of it and the sun's southern limb, from the vertex at noon, I found it to have 3'40" more north declination than the sun's centre, and at 3h.35m. afternoon I measured its distance from his next limb, 40"... determining its longitude from the sun's axis 66° and its declination from the solar equator 9°24' south. Whence, supposing the revolution ... performed in 25 days 6 hours, the angle of his equator and our ecliptic 7 degrees ... I designed the line of its way or trace over the sun, and the points in it where the spot would appear every morning after, at the same hour, till its egress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure meridional distances at standard times (noon), distance from solar limb, compute longitude and declination relative to the sun's axis/equator, adopt an assumed solar rotation period and geometric angles to predict the spot's trace and return. Confirm the theory by repeated observations and note morphological changes (apparent size/shape near centre vs limb).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for anatomical/case reports (polypus in heart)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person... died suddenly... some things material to our purpose... He died in the street suddenly; so that there cannot be expected so particular a relation of the symptoms... On opening the body, the liver ... the lungs were distended ... The heart much stretched ... polypous concretions also were found in the larger veins ... found in the right ventricle of the heart, and towards its apex firmly radicated ... The substance of the whole was plainly fibrous, resembling a nerve ... the reader may recur to the engraven figure ... The Explanation of the Figure of the Polypus, as it appeared when fresh expanded on a Board. Fig. A ... B ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include available patient history and reported symptoms; provide detailed dissection findings for each organ; give precise measurements, morphological descriptions, and textures; document location and attachment of lesions; provide engraved figures with labeled parts and an explanation; compare observations to prior authorities and discuss alternative explanations (e.g., post-mortem coagulation). Note limits due to incomplete histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and tests for identifying petrified wood (Lough Neagh stone)
rubrics_metrics.description: That what we call Lough Neagh stone was once wood, is most probable on these accounts: 1st, it will not stir with acids... 2dly, the Lough Neagh stone will burn and flame; and the smoke of it smells like the smoke of wood; 3dly, when burnt it betrays the very grain of wood, with the other vessels belonging to vegetables. ... I have many of them by me of various degrees of petrification ... I there discovered the whole body perfectly of the colour and grain of holly, as I can scrape it with my nail; but ... the discovery of the pith, as plainly and as perfectly distinct in colour and texture ... It is observed, that this petrifying quality is not equally diffused ... most strong about that part where the black water empties itself ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To judge whether a stone is petrified wood, perform acid tests (resistance to acids), combustion (does it burn and produce wood-like smoke), microscopic/macroscopic examination of grain/vessels and pith, and assess degrees of petrification. Test for magnetism (may be non-magnetic crude but magnetic when calcined). Note spatial variability of petrifying quality and consider species-specific susceptibility (e.g., holly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for reporting antiquities and a stratigraphic find (well at Kirkbythore)
rubrics_metrics.description: A well ... covered over with a plank ... above this was gravel and pavement ... Instead of walls there were two large wooden vessels, one on another, like hogsheads ... At the bottom about 5 yards deep, were 4 planks ... There was only found in the bottom Fabritian plate, old earthen vessels, ... several sandals ... The earthen vessels were of very fine texture, of a brick colour, and in several forms ... adorned with greyhounds ... inscriptions in Gothic characters ... The sandals ... leather fresh ... consisted of three principal parts ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the discovery context (exact location, cover, depth, relation to nearby features and stratigraphy), describe construction and materials of the structure (wooden vats, planks), catalogue artifacts with dimensions, decorative motifs, inscriptions and condition (repairs, soldering), and describe organic finds (sandals, leather) including construction details. Compare forms with regional types and publish illustrations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluating methods in geometrical construction (book review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author here shows how to construct all affected equations, not exceeding the 4th power, by the intersection of a circle and parabola, without omitting or changing any of the terms. ... of all lines of the first kind, a circle and parabola being the most simple, it follows that the way which our author has chosen is the best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mathematical construction methods by their generality (can construct equations up to 4th power), simplicity (use of simplest curves, e.g., circle and parabola), and by whether they avoid cumbersome preprocessing steps (such as removing the second term). Favor methods that keep original terms unchanged and reduce preparatory algebraic manipulation.
